summary: Ran the memory backfill CLI against 64 real sessions (60 pi-archive, 4 claude-code), writing 64 segments (6,408 messages, 9.0 MB) into .gizmo/memory/journal/. Verified idempotency by re-running (63 skipped, 1 new segment from this conversation's incremental growth), then confirmed typecheck, 168 passing tests, and clean formatting.
decisions: Switched Pi session reading from getEntries() to getBranch() so backfill reads the same source as live journaling, avoiding duplicated prose from retry/abandoned sibling entries
Recursive directory scan needed because Pi and Claude Code nest sessions in per-project subdirectories rather than a flat layout

Filtered Claude Code mechanical noise (<command-name>, <local-command-stdout>, caveat banners, <system-reminder> blocks) — they had been 7% of user sections, the most repeated text in the corpus; reduced to 2 of 344
Skip empty ## assistant sections that contain only a stop reason in the normalizer (also fixes live journaling)
Left genuine Pi duplicates (~1%, 2 of 344, where Pi records a re-sent prompt as two distinct entries) uncollapsed rather than editorializing source data
Imported segments tagged with source and trigger: backfill in frontmatter so the knowledge layer can distinguish imported history from live capture
errors: `pnpm --filter @gizmo/agent-server backfill` sets cwd to the package directory, so it scanned the wrong workspace and found 0 sessions; running from the repo root via `npx tsx apps/agent-server/src/memory/backfill-cli.ts` found 64
